Densifying a datetime64/timedelta64 SparseArray returns an object array mixing types: stored values are boxed by numpy as datetime.datetime (coarser units) or raw integers (nanoseconds), beside the pandas-boxed fill value. With an explicit dtype in to_dense, a nanosecond Timestamp/Timedelta fill is truncated to microseconds, and a fill whose unit differs from the column's is read as a raw integer under a numeric cast.

The dense result should match the dense (non-sparse) result: a single consistent type with the fill value normalized to a numpy scalar in the subtype's own unit, with no truncation of a nanosecond Timestamp/Timedelta and no raw-integer reading of a fill in another unit.
